mosaicanalysis.name: Mosaic Analysis: Grid Logic in Stone and Glass
mosaicanalysis.truth: Every mosaic encodes a symmetry group. The tesserae are data. The grout is the grid. The pattern is the algorithm made visible across centuries.
mosaicanalysis.qfep_connection: Classical mosaics are frozen algorithms. Roman opus tessellatum follows constraint-satisfaction rules indistinguishable from Wave Function Collapse. Byzantine gold-ground mosaics use wallpaper group symmetries that predate their mathematical formalization by a millennium. The lambda parameter lives in the tension between geometric perfection and material irregularity: hand-cut tesserae introduce noise that no shader replicates. QFEP reads this as the productive gap between F (the intended pattern) and E (the entropy of craft).
mosaicanalysis.formula: pattern = symmetry_group(motif, lattice) + material_noise(hand, stone, light)
mosaicanalysis.demonstration: Photograph a Roman mosaic floor. Identify the wallpaper group. Decompose the motif tile. Feed it to the pattern maker. Watch the algorithm reconstruct what craftsmen built by hand two thousand years ago â€” and see where it fails.
mosaicanalysis.description: Field study sequence connecting Italian mosaics, facade patterns, and ornamental systems to algorithmic pattern generation. From Pompeii's geometric floors through Byzantine gold-ground to baroque majolica, each map isolates a pattern system, identifies its underlying computational logic, and transforms it through the existing wallpaper group, WFC, and tessellation tools in Ada Research.
learning_objectives: Wallpaper group identification: recognizing the 17 groups in physical mosaics
Motif decomposition: extracting the fundamental domain from a repeating pattern
Constraint logic in tesserae: how adjacency rules in Roman opus mirror WFC
Color palette as data: mapping physical material palettes to algorithmic color spaces
Lattice types in architecture: square, hexagonal, and irregular grids in floors and walls
Noise from craft: how hand-cut irregularity differs from procedural noise
Baroque ornament as recursive grammar: L-system logic in scrollwork and volutes
Scale and viewing distance: how mosaic resolution maps to pixel density
